title: Rodrigues Has Batted 3, 4, and 5 in Three Consecutive Series. She Says She'll Bat Anywhere India Need Her.
excerpt: Jemimah Rodrigues's positional flexibility and Yastika Bhatia's return from injury give India options heading into the Women's T20 World Cup in England
body:
Jemimah Rodrigues has batted at No. 3, No. 4, and No. 5 across India's last three T20I series. She has scored runs at every position. And with five days to go before India's Women's T20 World Cup campaign opens against the Netherlands in Leeds on June 17, she wants the team to know that she will bat wherever they need her.

"I think I'm comfortable at all positions," Rodrigues said after the England series. "In the end, it is important for me to have clarity. And when I have clarity about a certain role, I know I can go out there and deliver."

That kind of flexibility is exactly what India need heading into a World Cup where the margin for error is thin and the conditions are unfamiliar.

## The England Lessons

India lost the three-match T20I series against England — a result that revealed both promise and problems. The batting unit showed depth: Rodrigues contributed consistently, Yastika Bhatia impressed on her comeback, and captain Harmanpreet Kaur delivered an unbeaten 56 under pressure in the final match.

But the bowling came undone at the worst possible moment. After reducing England to 38 for 3 in the decider, India watched Heather Knight and Alice Capsey put on 137 runs to chase down 181 with six wickets and nine balls to spare. Smriti Mandhana acknowledged the need to revisit bowling plans, saying the team would "go to the drawing board" before the World Cup.

The opening pair of Mandhana and Shafali Verma — reunited after Shafali's return to the squad — failed to fire in the series. Former selector Diana Edulji pointed to the openers as the primary area of concern. "It starts with the openers," she said. "If they don't give you a start, the middle order is always chasing."

## Bhatia's Comeback

One of the most encouraging developments has been Yastika Bhatia's return to international cricket after a lengthy injury layoff. Rodrigues spoke warmly about what Bhatia's presence means to the squad.

"Yastika was not with us lately because of her injury. So this is the only game time that she's also getting," Rodrigues said. "For us to have her here is a great advantage. We saw what she did in the first game, the way she batted. To come out after injury and do such a thing, it takes a lot of character."

Bhatia, who can bat in the top order and keep wicket, adds depth to a squad that had been stretched thin in her absence. Her ability to rotate strike and anchor innings from inside the powerplay complements the more aggressive approaches of Mandhana and Shafali.

## The World Cup Challenge

India are in Group 1 alongside Australia, Bangladesh, the Netherlands, Pakistan, and South Africa. Their tournament begins with a warm-up match in Cardiff before the competitive fixtures start on June 12.

The headline clash is against Pakistan at Edgbaston on June 14 — a match that Harmanpreet's team will approach with both intensity and recent experience. India also face South Africa on June 19 and Australia on June 22 in what promises to be a demanding group stage.

England's conditions will test India's pace bowling, which has been the team's weaker suit. Arundhati Reddy and Renuka Singh will need to find swing and accuracy on English pitches, while Deepti Sharma and Shreyanka Patil will be crucial in the middle overs.

## What NRI Fans Should Know

For diaspora cricket fans in the UK, this World Cup is the most accessible major women's cricket tournament in years. Matches are spread across Birmingham, Leeds, Manchester, and London, with ticket prices significantly lower than men's events. The India-Pakistan match at Edgbaston on June 14 is expected to draw a large South Asian crowd.

Star Sports and JioHotstar will broadcast in India and the subcontinent, while Willow TV covers the US and Canada. Australian fans can watch on Prime Video, and ICC.tv offers streaming in regions without a dedicated broadcaster.

India's squad: Harmanpreet Kaur (c), Smriti Mandhana (vc), Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Bharti Fulmali, Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (wk), Shree Charani, Yastika Bhatia (wk), Nandani Sharma, Arundhati Reddy, Renuka Singh, Kranti Gaud, Shreyanka Patil, Radha Yadav.
